$comment: M2 additions to the build kit's M1 OpenAPI document. See contracts/README.md.

changes.why: The served contract is the kit's M1 document plus these changes; it needs its own version so a client can tell them apart.

changes.value: Generated from the build kit's M1 contract plus contracts/overlay.json. Implemented detectors: MF-LINK-01, MF-ASSET-01. Contract only; an operation appearing here is not a claim that a deployment serves it.
changes.why: A reader landing on the generated file should know it is generated, and from what.

MF-ASSET-01 is implemented in M2, so a scan may request it, and may request both. The enum stays an allowlist: the four detectors that are specified but not implemented remain unrequestable. Widening only — every payload the M1 schema accepted is still accepted.

changes.value: Minimum role: operator. Phase: M1-M2. Membership, purpose, object and budget checks also apply. Detectors are limited to the implemented set. Contract only; not a claim this endpoint exists.
changes.why: The operation now admits two detectors; its description should say so rather than implying the M1 pack.

value.description: What the collector recorded about this observation: status, role classification, rendered outcome, timing. Only fields this system produced; never page content or scraped text.

changes.why: MF-ASSET-01 turns on facts the M1 Evidence shape had nowhere to carry: how an image was classified, and whether it actually painted. A reviewer cannot judge the claim without them, so they belong on the wire rather than only in the database.

Required rather than optional: an observation with no recorded detail is not evidence. This narrows a *response* schema, which is safe in a way narrowing a request schema would not be — the server always populates the field, and a client that ignores it is unaffected. generated-contract.test.ts enforces that distinction.

value.description: Detectors this deployment actually runs. The operator displays this rather than a constant compiled into its bundle, so the interface cannot claim a capability the server does not have.

changes.why: The workspace banner states which detectors are enabled. Deriving that from a value bundled into the client would let a stale bundle advertise a detector the server does not run; asking the server removes the possibility.

Required rather than optional: a session that does not say what the server runs would let the interface fall back to a guess. This narrows a response schema, which is safe — the server always populates it.

value.description: A commercial price in MINOR units of its currency. Deliberately not Money: Money carries provider cost in micro-units of the ledger currency, and the two must never be added. The differing field names make a mix-up a schema error rather than an arithmetic one.

changes.why: M2 adds the catalogue step between a confirmed finding and a quotation. The handoff contract has no shape for a priced scope, so the served contract needs one; adding a component schema cannot invalidate any payload the M1 contract accepted.

value.description: A catalogue entry at one version. Scope is defined by the catalogue; price is set by an owner approval. An entry with no approved price is visible but not sellable.

get.summary: Which catalogue scopes this case is eligible for
get.description: Minimum role: viewer. Phase: M2. Membership, purpose, object and budget checks also apply. Matching is deterministic against the venture catalogue; it never invents a price or widens a scope. Contract only; not a claim this endpoint exists.

200.description: Successful operation. Does not imply a later workflow step completed.

changes.why: The catalogue step needs a surface: read what a case is eligible for, draft one of those scopes, and withdraw a draft. These are new operations, not changes to existing ones, so every M1 call keeps behaving exactly as the handoff specified.

value.description: A condition about the customer that no capture can establish — authorized access, an agreed destination, a scope approval. Somebody records it and is named for recording it, the same shape as a review. Revoked entries are kept: what was claimed stays readable.

changes.why: Prerequisites decide whether an eligible scope is draftable, so the contract needs a shape for recording and revoking them. Additive: no payload the M1 contract accepted is affected.
